articles.title: My son’s back home – and my mothering skills have gone out of the window | Emma Beddington
articles.summary: Like many graduates, he has been forced to return to the nest. How will he cope with my pigeon chat and dodgy dregs for dinner? My graduate son has been back home for five months now.
body: Well, I can still wash, dry and fold multiple loads a week and ensure an uninterrupted supply of milk. It’s muscle memory, instinctive as breathing. I’ve lost other skills, though, like deciding what’s for dinner. I quit cooking the minute we dropped him off in halls in 2022 and wasn’t expecting to get my guns (guns = repertoire of five Meera Sodha recipes) out again. My husband and I have lost our conversational skills too, conversing in rambling, repetitive shorthand, and it’s unnerving having someone around to notice how much we talk about pigeons (constantly).
Of course, when he does escape, as older friends remind me, if I’m lucky I might get another last job after this last job: grandparenting.

articles.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Mae the labrador, who keeps me safe with her keen nose and piercing stare
articles.summary: Before getting her, I would fall, injure myself and then wake up alone. I’ve trained Mae to be a medical alert dog and she has helped me to embrace life again. It was love at first sight. I met Mae, a black labrador, in 2023 when she was 11 weeks old and she melted my heart completely.
body: At the time I was struggling with the physical and mental symptoms of my illnesses and needed a medical alert dog but there was a long waiting list. So I decided to train my own dog with the help of the Medical Detection Dogs charity.

Before Mae I would fall, injure myself and then wake up alone. Now Mae can tell based on my smell that a medical episode – when my heart rate drastically increases, causing me to pass out – is coming. She recognises my odour when I’m unwell and is given a treat so sees it as a fun activity. She alerts me either by giving me a very intense stare, or if I’ve missed that because my back is turned, she will escalate the alert by doing a very gentle jump up. She has even adapted her alerts to stare at whoever has got her lead so that they can tell me to take action.

If she’s feeling particularly cheeky when I come around after an episode, she’ll fetch her treat pot and toys so I can play with her, which is also quite relaxing. I can’t put into words how magical and calming it is to have this gorgeous dog staring at you and I think to myself: “I’m really lucky to have her in my life.”

articles.title: Is it true that … dock leaves cure nettle stings?
articles.summary: It’s a time-honoured treatment and rubbing certainly helps, but other leaves could be just as good. If you’ve ever brushed against a stinging nettle, chances are someone told you to find a dock leaf.
body: Probably not in any way that’s unique to the plant, says John Tregoning, a professor at Imperial College London and the author of Live Forever? A Curious Scientist’s Guide to Wellness, Ageing and Death.

When you brush against a nettle, tiny hairs on the plant can pierce the skin and release a mixture of chemicals, including histamine, acetylcholine and serotonin. These trigger burning, itching and redness.

Could dock leaves contain chemicals that counteract the sting, such as antihistamines? “Maybe, but probably not,” says Tregoning. There is little evidence that dock leaf sap contains substances capable of significantly relieving the reaction.

So why do people swear by them? Rubbing a leaf against the skin may provide a competing sensation that temporarily distracts from the pain, says Tregoning. “There’s a limit to the number of sensations that the nerve cells can process, so if you overstimulate them with the rubbing there’s less feedback from the pain.”
points: It’s a time-honoured treatment and rubbing certainly helps, but other leaves could be just as good.

articles.title: The hill I will die on: Nobody just ‘rustles up’ a lasagne | Keren Levy
articles.summary: We need to give up this pretence of effortlessness and start calling the dish what it is: a laborious meat-and-cheese architecture project. What is this “rustling up a lasagne” thing – apart from a straightforward contradiction?
body: I have a clear memory of the moment when, only recently out of our student years, a friend first pulled this misrepresentation out of her hungover hat. It was the day after a party, with a big clear-up under way and an agreed need for carbs. There was exhaustion, there were bin liners in hands, but she was busy “rustling”. And then, a mere few hours of laborious cooking and construction later, there it was on the table: the absolutely standard lasagne, in its “oh this old thing” white baking dish.

Decades later, the sheet-pasta extravaganza retains its reputation as an effortless standby, despite involving multiple components, careful assembly and a baking time long enough to watch a Netflix episode. You could be at the office picnic, an “everyone bring a course” dinner, even a wake, and people will casually announce they’ve made a lasagne as if they’ve decided to boil an egg, not committed hours to a meat-and-cheese architecture project.

“It’s no bother,” they add. “You can even buy the ready-made pasta sheets and do the cheat’s version. You don’t have to make it from scratch.” The relief. You’re still building the house, but someone’s delivered some bricks.

articles.title: The New Moon in Scorpio Has Arrived—Here’s What It Means for Every Star Sign
articles.summary: The second New Moon of autumn marks the start of a fresh lunar cycle, calling on us to manifest with intention—here, an astrologer explains what it could mean for you.
body: “The New Moon in Scorpio represents an intimate kind of beginning,” Bri Luna, founder of The Hoodwitch and author of Sex Magic For Dummies, explains. “Scorpio brings us into contact with sex, death, sorrow, and the appetites we keep private. Under this Moon, we may recognize how much of ourselves we’ve concealed to preserve a relationship or hold on to a life we’ve outgrown. There can be grief in admitting that, but also a renewed thirst for living. We can still want something deeply, even after disappointment.”

Internally, we are called to reshape and revitalize our daily lives. The urge to evolve into a more grounded, radiant version of ourselves is palpable. The rebirth we are undergoing invites us to shed old layers: like the metamorphosis from chrysalis to butterfly, real transformation takes patience before we can truly take flight.

articles.title: Anchovy-Garlic Pasta
articles.summary: A bagna cauda-inspired pasta for the brave.
body: Even those who swear they don’t like anchovies should be willing to take a “no thank-you” portion of this pasta. Sizzled with garlic, the tiny fish melt into a briny sauce that’s similar to bagna cauda, the warm Northern Italian dip whose savory quality comes from said anchovies. Instead of serving alongside crudités, toss this sauce with hot long pasta like linguine or spaghetti. No extra vegetables or protein needed, but I wouldn’t kick a salad with beans and bitter-slanting greens (kale, radicchio) off the table.

Cook fillets and oil from two 2-oz. tins oil-packed anchovy fillets, ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, and ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper in a large high-sided skillet or medium Dutch oven over medium-low heat, breaking up fillets with a wooden spoon or heatproof rubber spatula, until anchovies are melted and mixture is bubbling, about 2 minutes. Add 6 garlic cloves, finely grated, and cook, stirring often, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Remove pan from heat.

Cook 12 oz. long pasta (such as linguine or spaghetti) in a large pot of boiling salted water until very al dente, about 3 minutes less than package directions. Drain, reserving 2 cups pasta cooking liquid.

articles.title: As Podcasters Become Cultural Juggernauts, Brands Should Probably Tune In
articles.summary: As podcasters continue to sign deals with streamers like Netflix and Disney+ they are becoming valuable fashion talents for brands.
body: On a recent episode of Mary Beth Barone and Benito Skinner’s podcast, Ride, the hosts paused their conversation to talk about each other’s ’fits. “What is this kinda top?” Skinner asks, to which Barone replies declaring it vintage Miu Miu. Skinner goes on to cosplay an OOTD video, running through his full outfit: society archive T-shirt “vintage, of course”, vintage Ralph Lauren Polo shorts, and flip flops by The Row. Ride is not a fashion podcast with a capital-F, but this moment underscores why podcasts today — now largely streamed as videos — are becoming important platforms for fashion.

Brands are starting to take note. Skinner regularly sits front row at Prada, and has shot campaigns or content for Tory Burch, J.Crew and Ralph Lauren. Barone has attended the Tory Burch show for the last three seasons. And on the podcast, their brand deals include workout label Tonal, hair brand K18, and Bobbi Brown’s Jones Road.
points: As podcasters continue to sign deals with streamers like Netflix and Disney+ they are becoming valuable fashion talents for brands.

articles.title: From the Archives: When Iowa Governor-Elect Rob Sand Was Shot by Steven Meisel for Vogue Italia
articles.summary: Before winning Iowa’s gubernatorial race, Rob Sand was posing with supermodels, wearing Helmut Lang, and walking the Prada runway. Revisit his February 2004 Vogue Italia spread.
body: “Be My Baby,” by Steven Meisel, was originally published in the February 2004 issue of Vogue Italia.

With a fluffed-up quiff and a supermodel on his arm, here’s a look at Iowa’s next governor. Long before Democrat Rob Sand made political history, he was having a very different kind of moment in the spotlight, posing for Steven Meisel in the pages of Vogue Italia.

The year was 2004, and Sand was among the fresh faces who appeared in “Be My Baby,” an editorial in the February issue, photographed by Meisel and styled by Brana Wolf. Alongside Sand was a cast of rising fashion stars, including a young Caroline Trentini, with whom he posed in a series of moody, black-and-white portraits.

The concept centered on a romanticized vision of 1950s youth culture, abounding with the aforementioned rockabilly hair and lots of leather The original Italian introduction described the mood as a collision of bon ton —good manners and traditional propriety—and transgression.
points: Before winning Iowa’s gubernatorial race, Rob Sand was posing with supermodels, wearing Helmut Lang, and walking the Prada runway.

articles.title: No Time to Dye: Jacob Elordi Goes Blonde
articles.summary: Trading his natural brunette for a bleach blonde job, it looks like we’re set to see a big transformation for Jacob Elordi in A24’s “Scapegoat.”
body: The name’s Blonde. James Blonde. Kidding: it’s Jacob Elordi, who has just added another hairstyle to his ever-expanding beauty repertoire. The actor, whose dark, tousled hair has become almost as recognizable as his collection of Bottega Veneta bags, appears to have taken a trip to the bleach bottle.

In photos obtained by Deuxmoi, Elordi was spotted attending a performance of Paranormal Activity on Broadway in New York City on Saturday evening, alongside girlfriend Kendall Jenner. While the Australian actor (who is reportedly in the running to be the next James Bond) kept a low profile in a black beanie, there was no disguising the sandy blonde strands peeking out from beneath it. It’s a significant change-up from his usual chocolate-brown waves, though the hat leaves the full extent of his transformation something of a mystery.
